_meta.scope: Cuez Rundown web application UI elements (app.cuez.live) — STRICT SCOPE for this top-level key
_meta.scope_exclusions: This top-level key covers ONLY the Cuez Rundown web application. Cuez Storiez is a SEPARATE software product with its own UI surface (News Desk, Story Tray, Stories, Sub-stories, Dossiers, Publishing Points, News Feeds, Mailboxes, Story Categories, etc.) — NONE of those terms belong under this key. Cuez Gateway and MOStomator are also separate and excluded. Cuez Automator IS covered, but under a SEPARATE peer top-level key 'Cuez Automator' in this same file (the parser routes by Software Name input matching the top-level key). Browser-native UI (print dialog), Google Slides, and Intercom support widget contents are out of scope.
_meta.file_structure_note: This vocabulary file contains TWO top-level keys: 'Cuez Rundown' (this section) and 'Cuez Automator' (the desktop automation app). The pipeline's 'Software Name' input determines which top-level key is used as the canonical source. Each top-level key is self-contained and the canonicals do not cross-reference each other. Items with shared names (e.g. 'Block Row' exists in both, 'Play' button in both) are independent entries within their respective scopes.
_meta.v2_4_changes: Cross-referenced with the official Cuez Help Centre Cuez Lexicon (https://intercom.help/cuez/en/articles/6940949). Renamed 'Side Panel Details' → 'Side Panel View' to match the official term. Added new canonicals: 'Upgrade' button (top-right, opens plan selector), 'Confirmation Code' input (6-digit email confirmation field used in 2FA and account-locked flows), 'Locked Account' state (account locked after multiple failed login attempts). Added three new reference concepts to content_hierarchy: 'Heading' (collective term for Parts and Items), 'Badge' (generic block label), 'Action Menu' (generic 3-vertical-dots menu pattern). The lexicon confirmed nearly all existing canonicals as accurate.
_meta.v2_3_changes: Added 'Automator' button (and the Automator Pairing Screen it opens) to dashboard_elements — discovered via Cuez Help Centre's Automator Lexicon article, which documented the pairing flow originating from the Cuez Rundown dashboard.
_meta.notes: Canonical names for every user-facing UI element in the Cuez Rundown web app. British spelling ('Colour') used throughout. 'On Air' written without hyphen to match UI labels.
_meta.schema_v2_changes: Each entry now carries an explicit 'type' field. Canonicals have been stripped of redundant type suffixes (e.g. 'My Account Button' → canonical 'My Account', type 'button'). Names retain disambiguating context when the bare term would clash AND the types are also identical. The parser should pass canonical+type to the LLM as 'use these exact names with these types'.
_meta.v2_1_changes: Layout system corrected after tutorial audit: the toolbar layout selector is a single Layout dropdown with menu items 'Rundown only', 'Script only', 'Rundown & Script', and 'Tablet' (in shared view) — not three separate toggles as v2.0 modelled. Old toggle canonicals (Script Layout / Rundown Layout / Side-by-side Layout) kept as aliases on the menu items for backward compatibility. Added new canonicals for Edit Block Template View interactions (field rows, delete field, field visibility toggle, edit name pencil), Edit Field Modal expansions (Field Name, Cancel, Aa Uppercase/Lowercase/Original, Customize Option Popover, Option Name, Add field confirm), Create Block Template Modal, Block Visibility Filter Select All, media field Upload or Select File icon, dashboard Create new episode, toolbar Back, content structure + Add block, and Help Article Modal.
_meta.canonical_uniqueness: (canonical, type) together form the unique key for a UI element. The same canonical may appear with different types in different UI surfaces — e.g. 'Off Air Time' is both an input (toolbar field) and a display (timings column); 'Share' is both a button (toolbar) and a checkbox (prompter master/slave); 'Series' is both a folder (sidebar) and a reference (content hierarchy concept); 'Edit Field' is both a menu_item (action) and a modal (the dialog it opens). These intentional same-label-different-type duplicates accurately reflect the live UI and rely on the type field to disambiguate.
_meta.type_vocabulary: Types in use: button, icon, menu_item, input, checkbox, panel, dropdown, text, tab, canvas, list_item, toggle, slider, link, picker, container, state, badge, role, shortcut, layout, modal, counter, timer, countdown, indicator, display, bar, row, swatch, action, switch, view, folder, scope, colour_status, reference. The first 15 are taken directly from the tutorial extraction's element_type field; the rest are extensions for UI patterns the tutorial doesn't currently distinguish.
_meta.terminology_note: The live UI uses 'block template' as the visible label (e.g. 'Manage block templates', '+ Create block template', 'Edit block template'), while older Help Centre documentation uses 'block configuration'. Both terms refer to the same concept. Canonicals here favor the live UI text where it's clearly displayed; both terminologies are kept as aliases for narrator coverage.
_meta.support_widget_note: The Support Chat Panel that opens via the Support Chat Icon is rendered by Intercom (a third-party service), not by Cuez. Its internal tabs (Home, Messages, Help), category lists, and article links are out of scope. The Support Chat Icon and the Help Article Modal that opens from clicking an article are part of the in-Cuez chrome experience.
_meta.user_content_note: User-typed content (Episode names, Item titles, Part titles, organisation names, comment text) and user-configured Column instances (e.g. a column the user names 'Notes', 'Sound', 'EVS', 'GFX'), user-named Block Templates (e.g. 'PRESENTER A', 'PRESENTER B'), user-defined Label option values (e.g. 'Live', 'Replay', 'OFF', 'Portrait'), and user-named field rows (e.g. 'Title', 'Sound', 'Last Words', 'Type', 'Zoom', 'Link') are not Cuez UI elements and are not canonicalised. The CONTAINERS for that content (Episode Name, Part Row, Text Column, Field Row, etc.) are canonicalised. Default placeholder strings ('Untitled Part', 'Untitled Item') are also user-content surfaces, not canonical UI elements.

content_hierarchy._note: These are conceptual reference names for the entity hierarchy. They appear in narration but are not interactive UI controls themselves; the interactive controls are the rows, badges, and menus listed elsewhere.

aliases: block and columns configuration menu item

default_text_block_configurations._note: These are default Block Templates of type Text Block. They appear as labels in the Add Content menu and as badges on placed Blocks. The 'Prompter' default Text Block must be distinguished from the Prompter button (top toolbar) and the Cuez Prompter window — context disambiguates.

block_field_types._note: These are the field types selectable when configuring a Block Template field. Each appears as an option in the field type dropdown of the Edit Field Modal.

display_field_in_separate_row_checkbox.canonical: Display Field in a Separate Row
aliases: display field in a separate row checkbox
always display field in a separate row

columns._note: Column names like 'Notes', 'Sound', 'EVS' that appear in tutorials are USER-CONFIGURED column instances, not Cuez UI elements per se. They are added via the Add a New Column flow and labelled by users. Don't canonicalise specific user-defined column names.

views._note: Layout/view modes for the Episode Editor. The first three are toolbar toggles also represented in episode_editor_toolbar; here they represent the view mode itself as a state.

timings._note: Each entry here is a timing data field that can appear as a Timing Column. Values may be displayed inline in rows or in the Cue Overview Bar.

keyboard_shortcuts._note: Keyboard shortcuts are not visible UI elements but trigger actions on UI elements. Tutorial extractions targeting the action will typically reference the button/menu_item that the shortcut activates, not the shortcut name itself. These canonicals exist mainly for narration coverage when the narrator says 'use the bold shortcut'.

_meta.scope: Cuez Automator desktop application UI elements (Windows/Mac, runs at localhost:7070) — STRICT SCOPE
_meta.scope_relationship: Cuez Automator is a SEPARATE desktop application from Cuez Rundown. It is keyed under its own top-level entry in this vocabulary file. The pipeline routes by 'Software Name' input to the matching top-level key. Cuez Storiez and Cuez Gateway are still excluded as separate products. Cuez Media Player (CMP) is a built-in device type within Automator and is included here. Automator Satellite is a remote secondary instance — its UI mirrors the main Automator and reuses these canonicals.
_meta.v1_2_changes: Cross-referenced with the official Cuez Help Centre Automator Lexicon (https://intercom.help/cuez/en/articles/8166434). Renamed 'Panasonic' → 'Panasonic PTZ' to match official lexicon term. Added natural-phrasing aliases: 'neton.live' on NetOn.live, 'chyron-prime' (with hyphen) on Chyron PRIME, 'stream deck' on Elgato Stream Deck, 'ateliere' on Ateliere Creative Technologies. Removed redundant self-reference alias on UNO. Lexicon confirmed all device-type canonicals match the official supported integrations list.
_meta.v1_1_changes: Cross-referenced with the official Cuez Help Centre Automator Lexicon. Added two new device integrations: Resolume (graphics_engines, includes Avenue and Arena variants) and Calrec (audio mixing console). Added aliases for natural narrator phrasing: 'NewTek TriCaster' on TriCaster, 'Singular.live' on SingularLive, 'SPX' on SPX Graphics, 'Uno (by Singular.live)' on UNO, 'Companion' on Bitfocus Companion. The lexicon confirmed all existing canonicals as accurate.
_meta.notes: Canonical names for every user-facing UI element in the Cuez Automator desktop app. British spelling ('Colour') used throughout. Each entry carries an explicit 'type' field. The (canonical, type) tuple is the unique key — the same canonical may appear with different types in different surfaces.
_meta.type_vocabulary: Same type system as Cuez Rundown. Types in use: button, icon, menu_item, input, checkbox, panel, dropdown, text, tab, canvas, list_item, toggle, slider, link, picker, container, state, badge, role, shortcut, modal, counter, timer, countdown, indicator, display, bar, row, swatch, switch, action, reference. Automator-specific types added: device_type (for the 34+ device integrations selectable in the Device Type dropdown), function (for device action commands like Play/Pause/Stop), action_row (for individual rows in the Automation Action Rows panel).
_meta.user_content_note: User-typed content (Automator instance name, device names, macro names, variable names, step button labels like 'PLAY'/'STOP'/'IN'/'OUT', shortcut key labels, button names on CuezDeck) is not Cuez UI and is not canonicalised. The CONTAINERS for that content (Automator Name input, Device Name input, Macro Name input, Step Name input, etc.) are canonicalised. Hostname/Port/Token field VALUES are user content; the FIELDS themselves are canonical.
_meta.device_type_note: Per-device-type configuration fields vary widely (some need only Hostname; others need Hostname + Port + Token + Password). The 34+ supported device types are canonicalised by name with type 'device_type'. Their per-device-type configuration field combinations are not enumerated individually — generic field canonicals (Hostname, HTTP Port, TCP Port, Token, etc.) cover them.
_meta.function_note: The Function dropdown adapts to the selected device type. The standard cross-device functions (Play, Pause, Resume, Stop, Load Media, Load Template, Clear Layer, Clear, Set Opacity, Set Volume, Timecode) and System functions (System.Next, System.Previous, etc.) are canonicalised with type 'function'. Device-specific functions are not exhaustively enumerated.

conditions._note: Logic applied to action execution. The Condition dropdown selects between Always, If, and If Else.

automation_action_rows._note: Each row represents one device action. Has Device dropdown, Function dropdown, Input/Value, Delay, and a 6-dots menu.

steps_configuration._note: Steps create coloured sub-buttons in the Trigger Box. Each Step has a name, colour, optional visibility condition, and one or more automations.

cuezdeck_configuration._note: CuezDeck is a virtual button panel pinned to the top of the Automator screen. Three button types: Button, Status, Timer.

keyboard_shortcuts_panel._note: Configurable mappings of keyboard keys to automation function sets. Accessed via Gear → Keyboard shortcuts.

macros_panel._note: Reusable automation sequences. Accessed via Gear → Macros. Use Macros by selecting 'Macro' as device in any automation.

variables_panel._note: Two variable kinds: Normal (x) and AB-alternator (⇄). Accessed via Gear → Variables.

rundown_events_panel._note: Configure functions that auto-execute when opening an Episode. Same automation configuration interface as Block triggers.

media_handling._note: Per-device media auto-downloader configuration. Appears when 'Handles media' is checked.

device_types._note: The 34+ supported device integrations. Each appears as an option in the Device Type dropdown. Per-device-type configuration field combinations vary; the generic field canonicals above (Hostname, HTTP Port, etc.) cover them.

functions._note: Function names selectable in the Function dropdown of an Automation Action Row. The available functions adapt per device type. These canonicals cover the common cross-device functions plus System device functions.

automator_local_api_browser._note: Automator exposes a browser-based API explorer at localhost:7070/api/. Useful for debugging and learning trigger endpoints.

cuez_media_player._note: CMP is a browser-based playout endpoint that receives clips and images from the Automator. Built-in device type. Default port 7072.

automator_satellite._note: Automator Satellite is a remote secondary instance for distributed/multi-location production. Its UI mirrors the main Automator and reuses the canonicals above.
